newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Oct 5 Initial Claims from 319,000, Oct 5 4-Week Average from 332,250, Sept 28 Continued Claims from 2,501,000, and Sept 21 from 2,454,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial claims of 331,000 in the October 12 week.

The department said 11 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended October 5, the latest period for which the data are available. No states reported decreases in claims in this period.
States reporting the largest increases were California, with 5,361 new claims; Arkansas, with 2,613; Michigan, with 2,546; Florida, with 2,344; New York, with 2,287; and Pennsylvania, with 2,251.

California cited layoffs in the food and service industries and in agriculture. Arkansas had layoffs in the electrical equipment industry, and Florida had layoffs in construction, trade, manufacturing, agriculture and service industries.
Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the service, rubber, and plastics industries. Michigan and New York had no comment.
